title: Add the ability to set hierarchy of panels so that a panel can always overlap another panel
line: A vertical panel can now be set to take the screen corners, with horizontal panels making room for it.
explanation: Panels don't really overlap on Wayland: KWin lays out panels' reserved space in a fixed order, and since 2025 full-width horizontal panels always go first, so a top or bottom panel always gets the corners and a vertical panel always starts below it. There was no way to choose otherwise. A vertical panel set to "Fill height" now has a "Screen corners: Take over from horizontal panels" checkbox: when on, it extends over the horizontal panels' reserved strip (negative layer-shell margins) and full-width horizontal panels on that screen get a matching margin, so the vertical panel spans the whole height and the horizontal ones start after it. A small KWin fix makes this reliable: KWin could keep a stale panel size when the client applied an older configure after a newer arrangement.

commits.message:
shell: let a vertical panel take the screen corners

Horizontal panels always took the screen corners, so a vertical panel
could never reach the top or bottom of the screen. A vertical panel that
fills its edge can now take them, and horizontal panels move aside.

BUG: 520053

panel config: add an option for a vertical panel to take the corners

There was no way to choose which panel takes the screen corners when a
vertical and a horizontal panel meet. Vertical panels that fill their
edge now get a "Screen corners" checkbox in the panel settings.

BUG: 520053

layershellv1window: rearrange after the client changes its size

A client can apply an older configure after a later arrangement already
found its size right, and the surface then kept the wrong size. Arrange
again when the size changes with no configure pending, to fix it up.

BUG: 520053

---

media.caption: Master: the top panel always takes the corner, the left panel starts below it
Option on: the left panel spans the full height, the top panel starts after it

review.text: The result looks right in the screenshots, but it works around KWin's layer-shell arrangement order instead of changing it: the vertical panel uses negative margins to reach back over strips KWin already reserved, and plasmashell recomputes margins for every horizontal panel by hand. That depends on KWin's current horizontal-first order and needs plasmashell to recalculate in many places (thickness, exclusive zone, length mode, screen changes, panel removal). It will break quietly if KWin's arrangement changes. Who gets the corner is compositor layout policy, so it belongs in KWin. Separately, the plasma-workspace patch no longer applies on origin/master, and the KWin stale-configure fix is unrelated and should be its own MR.
changes: Implement corner priority in KWin's layer-shell arrangement (e.g. honour a per-surface priority/exclusive-edge hint, via org_kde_plasma_shell or layer-shell exclusive_edge, when ordering exclusive zones) and have PanelView just set that hint, dropping the negative-margin and horizontal-margin code
Rebase the plasma-workspace part on current origin/master
Submit the layershellv1window rearrange-after-size-change fix as a separate KWin MR with an autotest reproducing the stale configure
